current.unit: CLAIMING: A STABLE BASE-TILE PICK. Maintainer 2026-09-25: adding a tile to a set re-tiles half the world, and he edits those sets LIVE from the wiki (live/tuning/base_tile_sets.json), so he sees it. MEASURED: the pick is a walk over cumulative weights, so the total moves and every bucket with it — adding a 7th member to a 6-member set leaves only 50.2% of cells on their tile; a weight nudge, 92.0%. It IS deterministic (100% on a re-roll, no Math.random anywhere in tiles3 or render3). Fix is weighted RENDEZVOUS hashing: hash each member against the cell, keep the best — adding a member can only take the cells it wins. Measured 85.9% kept (optimum 85.7%) and 97.2% on a weight change, distribution and weight-proportionality intact. INTEGER-ONLY BY NECESSITY: member weights are fractional (0.05..30) so virtual-node replication is out, and Math.pow/log are V8-fdlibm vs CPython-libm and may differ in the last ulp — which would break cell-for-cell parity silently. So the score is a hand-rolled Q16.16 log2 over the FNV hash, compared by cross-multiplication in integers; proven BIT-IDENTICAL JS vs Python over 4000 rows. SHIPPED INERT: render3.py IS the spec (the fixture imports it) and basesets.mjs is a third implementation, so the rule may not flip in games2 alone. This lands the reference + vectors + gate with NO behaviour change, and requests the ports.

The corollary is a testing law: a saving that only applies when nobody is playing is a saving that changes what the developer sees, and he cannot test what he will ship.

THE RULE I BROKE TODAY AND WROTE DOWN: a server push restarts his world, and a restart costs him minutes of a world that looks destroyed while it re-streams — three in an hour is what made an ordinary loading weakness into an hour of rage. Batch them, and prefer the browser-code lane, which carried this fix in 33 s with no restart. THE DIAGNOSTIC LESSON: he told me the answer four times ('tabbed out and in and now it looks good') before I heard it — a symptom that a forced repaint cures is a REPAINT bug, not an asset bug, and I chased memory, then assets, then the service worker first.

notes.text: To every agent: while he is playing, BATCH your pushes. nangijala-deploy.yml triggers on games2/** and on every art domain, so any push - art, server or browser code - rolls a new Cloud Run revision and drops his socket. Measured tonight 17:49-18:07: six rollouts in eighteen minutes (4457-4460 monsters, 4461-4462 games-assistant). Each one restarts his world and re-streams everything on screen, and a client that loses one art request in that window keeps the hole until he restarts the app.

TONIGHT'S THREE LESSONS, all of them paid for by his evening. (1) NEVER push a board commit straight after a code commit: nangijala-deploy's `resolve` job skips a commit that is no longer main's head, and coordination/** triggers no deploy of its own, so the code silently never ships. Three of my pushes tonight never reached production, including one I told him was live. Code first, board only once the deploy run has left `resolve`. (2) A PUSH IS A WORLD RESTART for every agent: the deploy fires on games2/** AND every art domain. 17:49-18:07 ran SIX rollouts in eighteen minutes (4457-4460 monsters, 4461-4462 mine). Batch them while he plays. (3) MEASURE THE COST, NOT ONLY THE WIN. I cut ghost latency 416ms->52ms and never measured server CPU; EDGE_TICKS 2->1 plus a neighbour-wake rule made every room publish to every neighbour every tick, a world-scaled cost bought for a one-player benefit. Production then sat at 56-70% CPU with ZERO clients and stalled the event loop to 1.9s, which starved the SAME process's art serving and broke his game far worse than the boundary ever looked. Reverted in bbece9ba6c. NOTE for whoever takes the boundary next: the revert only halved the loop lag - ~56% CPU with nobody connected PREDATES tonight, and the standing suspicion is that one Node process running the authoritative 20Hz world should not also be serving ~50,000 art files.

ARTIFACT REGISTRY WAS 488 GB AND NOTHING HAD EVER DELETED AN IMAGE. Measured on his phone 2026-09-22 19:10: 'Repository Size: 488148.057MB'. Commit d54928100b measured 285 GB on 2026-08-15, so it grew +203 GB in 38 days = 5.3 GB/day. His billing export for 1-21 Sep: Cloud Run kr 240.81 list / kr 191.16 net (-17%, the fast lane working), Artifact Registry kr 181.73 (+41%) - the ONLY growing line, on course to pass Cloud Run and reach ~kr 509/month on its own within three months. Deriving from his own bill, the effective rate is ~kr 0.62/GB/mo. games2/deploy/ar-cleanup.sh existed since 2026-08-15 and had NEVER ONCE RUN: a fresh Cloud Shell opens as '(no project)', so DEVSHELL_PROJECT_ID and `gcloud config get-value` are both empty and the documented one-liner died on its first line - and its error told him to do something impossible (the paste PIPES the script, so there is no local file to name, and a PROJECT_ID=x prefix binds to curl, not to the bash across the pipe). NOTE ecf1fb9562, 2026-08-15, 'make the AR cleanup paste actually work from a phone': someone had ALREADY fixed this once, declared it fixed, and never ran it on a real phone. THE RULE: an ops paste is not fixed until it has been EXECUTED end to end by the person who has to run it - a script nobody can run is worth exactly nothing, and this one cost ~kr 126/month of standing spend plus ~kr 99/month more every month it continued. Fixed in 26be6eb3e3 (derives the project from `gcloud projects list`: one project is taken automatically, several hand back a ready line); both branches exercised against a stubbed gcloud before commit. The policy is now APPLIED server-side (keep newest 15, delete >14 days, dry-run off) and sweeps within 24h. Expected residual 10-25 GB, i.e. ~kr 10-20/month against ~kr 260 - and it needs CONFIRMING: re-read the size in 48h before anyone quotes the saving as fact.
